document: Create a law that requires unnecessary lighting to be turned off, Create a law that requires lights in shop window displays to be turned off at 1am. Interior lights in offices and other non-residential buildings should be switched off an hour after the last employee leaves., The impact will be to save wasted energy and reduce the impact of light pollution in the country, all of which damages wildlife, humans and the environment.

Stop the barbaric shooting of wild British birds., We oppose against the new guidance that allows the shooting of crows, jackdaws and magpies, so that game shooters can have their barbaric sport. , Protecting the interests of the elite.
They do not need to kill for food
This is merely an outdated barbaric game 
Clay shooting should be adequate …

Amend The Children's Act 1989 to include relationships with grandparents, in 2018 Justice Minister publicly said she consider if the need for a change in the law in relation to grandparents, stating the need for reforms clear that the system could work better. Nothing has progressed, help children maintain their right too safe, loving relationships with grandparents., Estimated 2 million grandchildren denied their chance to safe/loving relationships with grandparents, as those with parental responsibility are simply removing them from this valuable relationship. Children are impacted negatively being denied safe established contact and the law needs to be their voice. The impact of loss is not considered in family policy including amongst the judiciary which needs to be trained.1.4 million grandparents are affected & many have horrifying judicial experiences.

Fund blood tests for all women going through the menopause, The Government should provide funding to ensure that all women going through the menopause have access to blood tests to measure their hormone levels, to help inform decisions about hormone replacement therapy (HRT)., The menopause can effect the hormones of women in different ways. A blood test should be available for each women going through the menopause, which could help doctors decide on any appropriate hormone replacement therapy (HRT).

Develop an Education Health Care Plan template for use by all local authorities, As part of forthcoming & long awaited SEND Review the Government should develop a single national template for EHCPs, following consultation, including with parents and school leaders., We believe a standardised template, developed following consultation, would be helpful to families, if this was simplified, especially where they have children attending school/ college in different LAs. It should also support settings / leaders who have children and young people from different local authorities in their establishment. It should also better enable the Government / inspectorates to quality assure the quality of EHCPs across local authorities.

Introduce Witness Personal Statements in line with Victim Personal Statements, I am encouraged that progress has been made in giving Victims a voice in relation to how an offence has affected them & in turn the impact on sentencing. Witnesses are not afforded the same considerations, and I want all witnesses to be able to give a personal statement., Victim Personal Statements enable Victims to explain how they have been effected by an offence, incorporating the physical, financial & emotional.
 
I want witnesses to be given a right to make their own personal statements, to give them a greater voice in the criminal justice process.

Bring down the price of gluten free goods, The price of gluten free food in supermarkets more than doubles the price of food containing gluten. The brands that are cheaper are not very nice. Warburtons gluton free tiger loaf is £3.50 as opposed to a regular tiger loaf which is £1.00, Lentil crisps cost £1.80 per packet where as a share bag of regular quavers costs £1.00 

I'd love more research to be done into how we can lower the cost of these products to make the good quality things more accessable to people without a large amount of discretionary income

Ban plastic bags in the UK, Single use plastic bags are problematic, taking up to 1000 years to biodegrade; even then they still exist as micro plastics. We need the government to ban plastic bags in order to try and help the current climate change issue to which these plastic bags are contributing majorly to., We need to act now, before it’s too late. Plastic bags hinder the quality of our earth, despite it only being the start. We as the UK, need to start being more responsible for our actions on how we’re damaging our earth. Although you might think this won’t change anything, it’s a start. A start to make our world a better, environmentally friendly world. Please share this to everyone you can so we can try and out a stop to climate change once and for all. Thank you

Require MPs and civil servants report all contact with corporate entities, Maintain a publicly-accessible list of any contact made between (or on behalf of) corporate entities (including charities) and MPs or civil servants. MPs and civil servants should be legally required to report all such contacts, and failure to do so should be an offence., We believe corporate lobbying is a thorn in the side of a healthy and productive society, and can create an uneven playing field and corrode the integrity of the institutions this nation relies upon. Whilst coordinating with the corporate world is an essential element of the valuable work MPs and civil servants perform, transparency of such engagements is essential to maintain public trust in the government, and the democratic process of this nation in general

Give more house back to locals and less holiday lets, Cornwall and Devon area, The housing crisis in Devon and Cornwall are because of air b&bs and more people renting their properties out for holidays makers, meaning less long term properties for people, single, couples, families even the older generation. Meaning less people to work and contribute to the economy, Close some of the air b&bs about half or more and make sure that the people who are renting out as a holiday let have to pay abit more for council tax to help benefit Devon and Cornwall, hopefully freeing up housing for the locals to ease the pressure of the housing crisis

Ban hospital from stopping both parents from being with their children., The government should make it impossible for paediatric and neonatal wards from denying both parents access to their children while they are in hospital. As it stands on most wards. Only one parent is allowed in at a time despite family circumstances., During the covid pandemic, hospitals have quite rightly had to in-force some tight restrictions. But denying any parent access to their child is unacceptable in any circumstances. Some hospitals have been preventing both parents from being with their child causing a significant amount of depression and stress. Parents cannot ‘visit’ their own child. Parent and child’s well-being has been dramatically impacted and not always taken in to consideration. I am now asking the uk government to stop it.

Withdraw from the Paris agreement related to climate change, The Paris Agreement is a legally binding international treaty on climate change., Its goal is to limit global warming to well below 2, preferably to 1.5 degrees Celsius, compared to pre-industrial levels.
 
I am asking the Government to pull out of this agreement.
 
I believe the government has been spending too much money on providing cleaner energy, which is a problem when the national deficit is too high. An example is subsidies to those building wind turbines. I believe this Paris agreement is influencing road taxes for car users as the Government tries to meet its climate goals. Also, businesses may face higher taxes, later on, to pay back the national deficit. I believe that to improve our economy and financial well-being we need to pull out of the Paris agreement.

Lower family court fees, I feel that the price of the family court fees is extortionate and should be lowered to an affordable amount to allow more fathers and mothers to help gain access to their children., On top of court fees, solicitor fees are also expensive when you work pay rent etc. Some parents in this situation have to work two jobs to help cover court fees and solicitor fees, which can affect people’s mental health and cause them to feel like they want to give up.

payments given by mps through expenses to be means tested Inc. utility bills, The government should introduce Means tested expenses and remove all utility bills and council tax from being a claimable option 
Also the removal of subsidised food and alcohol from Parliament to be replaced by means testing, This government has no understanding of the cost of living crisis due to silver spoon syndrome , 
We find it repugnant that at a time of hardship, mps who clearly have the ability to pay their own way choose to claim it through expenses costing the tax payer,millions in subsidies, one such mp claimed £225,000 in a year 

The government should do this because they have no trust from the British people due to successive governments need to tax the poor an destroy publicly owned ventures

Require public referendums to approve participation in any armed conflict, There should be a formal requirement that the majority of UK voters should be in agreement before starting or joining any Armed Conflict. This agreement should be based on a public referendum, as their MPs are under no obligation to vote according to their constituents' wishes., Wars kill, maim and destroy. People lose lives, people are injured and livelihoods shattered. We believe the only winners are arms companies.

Given the magnitude of commencing or becoming embroiled in armed conflicts, the UK Government should seek the explicit agreement of its voters. Currently, the convention is that the House of Commons should have the opportunity to debate the deployment of military forces, prior to doing so, except in the event of an emergency.

The Commons derives its power from the people. The people need to be heard.

Extend the Leasehold Reform Act to ground rent on existing residential leases, Prior to the Leasehold Reform Act, the freeholders could set ground rent at whatever amount they chose. New protections do not extend to existing property owners. Many current leaseholders have found they are unable to sell as mortgage firms and banks may not approve lending on such properties., The distinction between new leases and old leases puts current owners at a competitive disadvantage.

Create a law  to regulate the way used catalytic-converters are sold as scrap., Make it harder for the thief to sell stolen catalytic-converters. I want a traceable line of where they have come from,  including vehicle ownership details and the scrap catalytic-converters  only to be bought from registered company's licensed to sell them as scrap., I want a traceable line of where they have come from,  including vehicle ownership details and the scrap catalytic-converters  only to be bought from registered company's licensed to sell them as scrap. Also large fines for scrap dealers handling stolen catalytic-converters. This could put an end to catalytic-converter theft which has seen a massive increase due to the ease of selling them. This could also help with reducing insurance claims.

Regulate wildlife food so it’s safer for hedgehogs, and all mammals & birds, Shockingly there are currently no regulations on foods sold to be given to wildlife. These foods can contain ingredients that are unsuitable or even harmful., We are calling on the Government to regulate these products, so only foods that are suitable for particular animals can be sold as such.
 
Sadly, well-meaning people are buying products labelled as food for particular animals, but they often contain ingredients that can cause the animals that eat it health problems, or even death. We are therefore calling on the government to regulate these products.
 
On 30th July 2020, hedgehogs were added to the Red List for British mammals and classified as vulnerable to extinction. Ensuring food sold as suitable for hedgehogs is safe could help protect this species.

Reduce the cost of Animal Health Certificates, Investigate the following and overly expensive system for transporting domestic pet's to and from Europe. When in the EU, we paid £40 approx. for a three year pet passport. Now, with Brexit, it will cost over £200 and more for a four month AHC.
Thankyou., This should have been discussed during Brexit negotiations

Hold a referendum on re-joining the EU on previous terms, It is time that we ask people again if they would like to re-join the EU. Some in society have realised that they may have been mistaken, and that they may have been lied to., Public opinion has changed drastically and we suggest holding an online poll to find out if this nation firstly wants a referendum to ask the question, the results of this poll would oblige us to have a national referendum to decide if we ask to re-join our friends across the EU.

Require local authorities obtain DBS checks before licensing Tattoo Artists, Local Authorities should be required to do DBS checks on Tattoo Artists before granting licenses, to identify past offences. The decision of whether to grant a licence would be on a case-by-case basis (minor/non-violent crimes should not exclude tattoo artists)., Tattoo artists are in a position of power, with a client.
 
Tattoo processes are often intimate experiences, close contact, sometimes in an isolated space alone with the artist and people should be able to be confident that they are safe.
 
Too many people have been abused within this industry; clients AND other tattoo artists. We must do better to protect them. Requiring DBS checks tis one step closer to being a safer, inclusive industry.

Increase funding for existing and new youth clubs, The Government should direct additional funding to local authorities for youth services. Closure of youth clubs has been linked to increased youth violence, and increasing funding for these services could help protect children's future., Poverty and inequalities in the UK are real, but also greatly hidden and misunderstood.
 
Employment opportunities and positive role models are scarce. As we edge closer to post-pandemic, the effects of Covid-19 still remain. Young people were one of groups most disadvantaged by the pandemic. From school closures, to minimal social interaction in formative years, to a lack of resources for lower income households. Directing funding to youth services is a vital first step.

Allow parents access into nursery settings, Allow parents access to nursery setting, even if this is staggered and intermittently., Children that joined nursery in 2020 will be the only kids to fully suffer this loss. Having gone 2 years with no parent access to nursery. Those that joined primary school in august 2021 had parent engagement in their first nursery year (2019/20) and they have suffered massively in their first year of primary 
Those who joined nursery 2021 have another year to hope for parent engagement.

Enforce CMS /CB to do more checks if child is actually attending education, Currently there is massive loopholes where a parent with care can claim child benefit and child maintenance without any proper checks in place. The cms have openly admitted they only call the resident parent. This is not a proper investigation, This simple check at the start and mid term could save the government money by not paying unnecessary child benefit. Child benefit do not check that any children are actually attending colleges etc

Make property offers legally binding like in Scotland, The Government should make the buying and selling of property fairer by making offers legally binding in England and Wales. This should put a stop to gazumping once an offer has been accepted. , House prices are rising, along with the cost of living making it impossible for first time buyers and buyers with a budget. Schemes such as “help to buy” and “part ownership” are heavily flawed and do not do enough to support the buyer, particularly when you come to sell. It is currently legal for a buyer to have an offer accepted (in an already sparse market and usually above asking price) to then be heavily gazumped by a cash buyer who may not even plan on living there.

Stop all post Brexit payments to the EU, Leave means leave. The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) has estimated that the UK will be paying the 'Brexit divorce bill' until 2064.
 
We demand all post Brexit payments to the EU stop now.,

Extend Help to Buy scheme to people who have previously owned a home abroad, I want the Government to help people who have previously owned a home abroad to be afford a home in the UK. Many immigrants spend their savings to relocate. Where someone has purchased but then sold a property abroad we would like to be considered as first time buyers for the Help to Buy scheme., Immigrants that have previously owned a home abroad cannot access the Help to Buy scheme, and many will never realize their dream of owning their own home, no matter how hard they work.
 
Please change this scheme to include people who have previously owned property abroad, to help them buy a home in the UK.

Prohibit the unsolicited delivery of plastic bags, The Government should prohibit the delivery of plastic bags, where these have not been requested. Many charities bulk mail plastic bags, for use to give donations, to households across the country. This contributes to harm against the environment, and can also be a risk to pets., The world is trying to reduce its use of single-use plastic, and the British public are now charged for single-use carrier bags in supermarkets. However on an almost daily basis some charities post single-use plastic bags through people's doors, which are unsolicited. This is bad for the environment and a risk to pets.
 
This is at odds with the charge on plastic bags in supermarkets and should be addressed, both to reduce nuisance mail and to protect the environment.

Ban adverts for charity on TV, We believe there are too many charity adverts on television, requesting donations or even to be included in people's wills. We want the Government to ban adverts for charities on TV, as these adverts often instil guilt, and can affect viewer's mental health., We believe that charity adverts should not be on television. It can be exhausting to see so much negativity and adverts using disturbing visuals and footage to encourage people to donate to charity. Some charity adverts use actors, which we believe is misleading.

Set the date of the next General Election for 2 May 2023, We want the next General Election to be set for 2 May 2023, so the British people can vote then. The next General Election could be as late as 2025. We want the Government to guarantee this will happen on 2 May 2023 now, to give candidates time to prepare for the election., Under the Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act, Parliament will automatically dissolve five years after it first sits, unless the Prime Minister requests a dissolution from the sovereign. We believe a General Election cannot wait until 2025, or even 2024.

Make polyamorous marriages legal, Make it legal for people in consenting polyamorous relationships to get married., I want this to be legal because it currently is not and so people in polyamorous relationships are unable to marry their partners, despite the fact that their relationships are just as "normal" to them as a monogamous one is to others. It is wrong that they are unable to marry the people they love due to the fact that are not monogamous.

Extend the help to buy scheme beyond March 2023, Extend the help to buy scheme for new builds and first time buyers after March 2023 to still give people a chance to get on to the property ladder., To give people a chance to get onto the property ladder by having help to buy and 5% deposit for longer. Too many first-time buyers are struggling to get a full deposit for a house, and this is particularly difficult for those wanting to start a family. This would help more families and first time buyers if it was extended.

Make the period of Ramadan a school holiday, The Government should introduce a new school holiday for the entire month of Ramadan. Christmas is a holiday for everyone, including Christians, meaning time off school. But as a Christian, I feel Muslims should get time off too!

, It’s not fair on Muslims. Fasting is a very tiring thing especially as they do it for long periods a day.

Review guidance on use of masks in residential care homes, The Government should review guidance which says that face masks should be worn by all care workers and visitors in care settings. Managers of care homes should conduct their own risk assessments and then decide whether masks should be worn., The disparity between general population, visitors to care homes and residents and staff of care homes is no longer justifiable. Our residents are struggling and staff are finding it hard to provide best care. Mask use is a literal barrier to making connections, communicating and sharing emotions. Residents should be involved in any decision-making around mask wearing in their care settings.

Question the minister for DEFRA over lack of action halal and kosher labelling, There have been 2 parliamentary petitions on labelling for halal and kosher with nothing of substance resulting. In response to the 1st (1) they said after Brexit we'd have more opportunity to label. For the 2nd (2) there was a consultation. Nothing has changed. We demand the minster be questioned., The Parliamentary Petitions committee has the power to summon a minister for questioning. It is strictly forbidden for many Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists or Christians to consume any halal or kosher certified material. We ask for clear prominent labelling so we can make a clear choice. We demand the committee bring the Minister for DEFRA to be questioned on this. 
(1)  https://petition.parliament.uk/archived/petitions/229231
(2) https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/565002

Get the prices that Out of Hours Veterinarian services charge regulated, Currently, a lot of Out of Hours and Weekend Veterinarian services charge extortionate fees for consultancy.  These fee's are enormous in comparison to a week day fee, and in some cases over 5 times more expensive the normal rate.  We would like to see this regulated., Pet ownership is already an expensive thing.  On a normal day, a visit to the vet would cost on average £100 for a small issue.  If your pet is unwell out of business hours, there is no choice but to use this service and pay these extortionate rates to help your pet.  The alternative is for the owner to see their animals suffer.  We would like to see these fees regulated and made affordable.  This would also help to get pet insurance prices to drop as the payouts would be lower.

Stop the sale of Channel4, The Tory sale of yet another national asset needs to stop. It is publicly owned then it should be for the public to decide. 

The Government have no mandate for this. They act on our wishes, not the other way around

If we don't state now not to do it the BBC will be next., An asset that runs itself successfully at profit, has no agenda, creates jobs.

In the era of fake news owned by one old austrailan bloke quality independent news is even more important.

The sale can't guarantee who will buy channel 4 or their agenda. Much like football clubs our media industty could become a play thing of oligarchs, look how that's working out now. 

Any profit will not be invested back into programmes but into owners pockets at a detriment to the UK audience.

Stop Privatisation of publicly-owned Channel 4, Leave Channel 4 as a public-service broadcaster owned by the British public and funded by ads, taking into account their already submitted financial proposals and retaining their unique public-service model going forward., Everything that makes Channel 4 so unique and special to work for is in their public ethos, even though they’re funded by ads. C4 is entirely financially solvent as it is, pandemic notwithstanding, and it is the breadwinner of 100’s of small indies, without whom an entire employment eco-system in the regions wouldn’t exist. The TV industry and the public do not want this. This is OUR public service broadcaster and we do not want it to become yet another faceless profit machine.

Scrap plans to privatise Channel 4, Channel 4 is under threat. The government plans to sell the publicly  owned channel to a private buyer. This will seriously damage the creative sector, affecting how much the channel spends in different UK regions - undermining its remit to reflect interests of different communities across the UK., Each year Channel 4 works with around  300 creative companies across the UK to develop incredible programmes like recent dramas Help, It's a Sin and current affairs show Unreported World and has helped develop the UK’s creative sector into a global force. its unique model - commercially-funded but with a public benefit remit – allows the Channel to commission programmes that showcase Britain in all of its diversity and its privatisation would seriously undermine this and must be stopped.

Revoke the non domicile status that allows residents to avoid paying U.K tax, Revoke the non domicile status, Because they are tax resident in the UK, non-doms will typically not be tax resident in their country of domicile, and therefore not liable for tax in either country, this status allows the very rich to avoid paying tax to the U.K, this anomaly should be revoked as soon as possible as it prevents significant sums being collected by HMRC.

Make zero hour contracts illegal, The blanket phrase ‘zero hour contract’ allows many ways for companies to word ‘we can’t guarantee you any hours’ and in my opinion it is a really abused system! Hard-working employees should be allowed the guarantee of a set number of hours per week in return for the work they provide., I believe it should be mandatory for every company to guarantee each of its employees at least 16 hours of work per week. Too many managers abuse the power of the ‘zero hour contract’ and give their employees barely enough hours to afford food and clothing for their children … it is a joke!

Apply to join the European Free Trade Agreement (EFTA), Apply to become a member EFTA along with Lichtenstein, Switzerland, Norway and Iceland, to allow for free trade between the UK and Europe., Brexit has added unnecessary red tape to the system and has damaged the UK economy. EFTA will allow the UK to trade freely with Europe, without the additional burdens of EU membership. This should boost the British economy and trade and solve the issues relating to the NI protocol and the Brexit deal.

Allow children of dependent parents of an EU citizen sponsor to come to the UK, Change Home Office policy so as to allow children of dependent parents of EU citizens to join them in the UK through the EU Settlement Scheme., The relevant legal provisions (Appendix EU and Appendix EU (Family Permit)) allow for certain family members of EU citizens to join the latter in the UK. This includes their children, certain partners and dependent parents. 
But, there are shortfalls that lead to absurd, unfair and harsh consequences. For example, a minor child of a dependent parent of an EU citizen sponsor is not permitted to join their parents and sponsor under either appendix.
It is crucial, therefore, that this is changed.

Legalise the use of Escooters, I want transport ministers to consider slight easing of the ban on private escooters on public roads., I think with some careful regulation of Escooters there could be a way to allow privately owned escooters to be used on public roads while minimising injuries to pedestrian and the riders. 

Right now a lot of people are still relying on they're cars because they can't use they're escooters due to the law banning they're use in public. There is a lot of environmental benefits to legalising they're like cutting down on car use therefore reducing emmisons.

Stop the bedroom tax, Things need to change to help low income families.

With the price of everything from power, petrol, water, income tax to food all going up but wages and benefits not matching these rises we are seeing more and more people/families struggling to pay for those things, Stopping bedroom tax would be a step in the rite direction for those on low incomes and on benefits in council property. 

We as a nation are not doing enough for those on low incomes where some end up on the streets because of not being able to pay for rent etC. It is so bad some have to use food banks, stopping the bedroom tax would mean that those in council property would have a little more money if they did not have to pay the tax. Things need to change to help low income family.

Remove the restrictions on keeping Siberian chipmunks, The Government should remove all restrictions on buying and owning Siberian chipmunks, and should leave any international agreements which constrain this. We don't believe that Chipmunks cause an environmental hazard , and that they can be a great pet with therapeutic benefits.,

Stop nurserys charging parents for days they are closed, eg Bank Holidays., As a human right, we shouldn't have to pay for a service we are not getting. With the cost of living increasing and the average cost a day being £50+ to put your child into a nursery. Why are we paying for a service that can't physically be used when the nursery is closed. Stop bank holiday charges!,

Make it illegal for over 18s to engage in sexual activity with under 18s, We want to prevent sexual exploitation of 16-17 year olds, recognising young people at this age are vulnerable to grooming & exploitation by adults. This petition asks the UK govt. to better protect 16-17 year olds by making it illegal for adults to engage in sexual activity with any under 18s., It is currently legal for anyone over 18 to have sexual contact with a 16 or 17 year-old - unless they are in a 'position of trust' and the child is in their care. That adult could be a ’family friend’ who has the trust of a child’s parents/carers and has known the child their whole life.

We want the UK Government to appoint a dedicated Minister for Manufacturing., The strength of the UK economy, its ductility, resilience, and agility are directly dependent upon a flourishing manufacturing sector.
Our sector will be at the heart of the Government's Levelling Up agenda.
To ensure success, we need a dedicated Minister to represent our needs, and be our voice., We are the life blood and foundation of British industry and yet we currently do not have a dedicated Minister within Government to represent us. 

Our contributions to the economy are:
o	£183 billion output
o	2.5m jobs
o	51% of all exports
o	64% of all UK R&D 
o	15% of all business investment
o	12% higher wages than average

99% of all manufacturing businesses employ less than 250 people and are classified as Micro or SME's and yet our voices are rarely represented or heard. 

We need a voice.

Work internationally to create fully digital animal export/import certification , The Government should work with other countries, particularly the EU, to create an entirely digital animal export/import certification system. Since Brexit, movement of animals in and out of the UK has become a long, expensive, prone to error process, confusing and unnecessarily expensive., Certain documents which need to be exported with the animal require from 9 to 27 pages, and hence it’s not environment friendly either. This could all be avoided using an online certification system.

Establish an online certification system that permanently removes the need for physical paper documents to travel with the animal.

This could make exporters, vets, owners and govt workload slimmer and less prone to errors in the documentation.

Not to raise staff ratios in early years, Look at “free childcare” not ratios. The amount the nurseries get funded for child care does not cover staff wages or consumables at all. Settings charge extra to meet these costs. Stop treating early years educators as babysitters, we do not just supervise children, we educate and care for them!, The ratios in early years are there for a reason. Raising the ratio will mean staff will leave the profession due to stress and workload. Early years staff are underpaid and stressed already, the Pandemic has seen nurseries closed and staff leaving to do less demanding jobs. 
There needs to be a change in the way the government sees early years education, especially in deprived areas. We educate, care and safeguard the children in our settings and it’s hard enough without higher ratios

Free NHS Prescriptions for 18 Year Olds and over in Full Time education, Free NHS Prescriptions and all other services, such as, dental care, sight tests, funding for vision instruments, wigs and fabric support must be given to those who are 18 years and over within Full Time education, Costs of living are highly increasing, due to the current pandemic and war. Which affects all, but severly effects students who sruggle to pay for countless expenses, such as, Shopping for Food/toiletries, Accommodation, Travel. Some students also deal with dangerous levels of stress caused by studies which they require therapy to ease their situation.

Reffering back to the current world, where Coronavirus is still present and cases/deaths are increasing as well as the current crisis. Health is manditory, which does effect many in daily life as well as students who suffer on a day to day basis. By providing Free NHS Prescriptions, and other services listed above will support students. Which includes myself. Who are in need of this crucial service.

UK gov buildings should be mandated to fly the Union Flag all year around., UK government buildings are only encouraged to fly the Union Flag all year around. 

https://www.gov.uk/guidance/designated-days-for-union-flag-flying, I'm proud to be British and the flag of a proud, sovereign nation should be on display at all times.

Offer Children that attend a school nursery first refusal on reception placement, Allow children that attend a schools nursery to have first refusal on reception places. Not just based on catchments, Children that attend a schools nursery will have made friendship groups, will have become accustomed to the schools ways and timetables, will be used to teachers and the surrounding. For some children this may have taken a long adjustment period. Many also have the schools uniform. To then be refused a placement and to have to adjust to this all over again in a new setting is unfair to both child and parents.

Ban children from all greyhound tracks, The Government should ban children from attending greyhound racing tracks. At these tracks there is a risk of children’s involvement in placing bets with their parents. , Around 55,000 problem gamblers are aged 11 to 16 in the UK, according to the Gambling Commission, with a further 85,000 estimated to be at risk. Children are susceptible to both family and peer influences and marketing campaigns. Children’s charity BigDeal say that if children accompany peers and parents who are gambling, the chances are higher that the child will develop a gambling problem themselves. If we remove children from these situations we help to safeguard them from future addiction and harm.

Extend Ofsted regulation to all after-school clubs, with annual inspections, Many after-school clubs are not regulated and of those that are, only 10% are inspected a year, meaning a provider may not be inspected for nearly a decade., We want the Government to require all providers of after-school clubs to register with Ofsted, and be subject to annual inspections.
 
More than 80 safeguarding referrals have been made about clubs in school grounds in the past five years, according to information requests made by the BBC.
 
There is nothing more important than protecting our children. We believe the swiftest, most effective way of doing this is greater regulation. Leaving children in the care of unregulated individuals without any inspection is unacceptable. The effects of abuse can impact children for the rest of their lives.

Make Misogyny a Hate Crime, Make Misogyny a hate crime. I know this has been recently rejected, but woman have to step forward and urge for a change., Misogyny is a terrible thing. In the USA, for example, 81% of women have experienced some sort of sexual harassment. We need to stop this now.

Debate bringing in 100% Mortgages for long term renters., Where someone has been renting for a minimum period of 24 months continuous, the rent paid should be considered satisfactory proof of affordability for a mortgage with 0 deposit.  

Example: Someone paying £750 per month for that period, should be able to get a mortgage at the same monthly rate., A lot of the UK’s population have more than enough income to afford a mortgage but don’t have the disposable income if they are also having to pay rent.

This would make a massive difference to get people on the ladder and also aid the house buying market in the UK.

It’s a very simple concept, how do you expect someone to save £500 a month towards a deposit if they are also already forking out their wages on rent. 🤷‍♂️

Make home sellers liable for costs incurred by buyers if they pull out, Buyers can spend hundreds of pounds thinking the property sale will go ahead. , If the Seller pulls out before the exchange of contract, they should be liable for the these costs such as valuations and surveys which cost £100 or more and any other cost spent by the buyer thinking the sale will go ahead.

If 10 sellers pull out of the sale before contract exchange,  a single buyer could potentially lose thousands on valuations, solicitors' and mortgage advisers fees etc.  The buyer's bank lending the mortgage will also conduct a hard search against the buyer's credit file which can contribute to a lower credit score.  It's not fair.

Suspend any MPs accused of sexual offences pending investigations, Given the number of allegations occurring of a serious nature we believe there is the need for any MP or Minister formally accused of sexual offences to be suspended from the House, and any ministerial posts, pending the conclusion of all relevant investigations., To establish a formal process whereby any MP or Minister is suspended immediately from the House and any ministerial posts, pending completion of all relevant investigations - by the police, government or parliamentary authorities - so as to safeguard the public, and others within Parliament and Government.
 
The removal of an MP against whom allegations of this kind are made should not be a personal choice after a formal allegation is made, but a requirement.

Allow European Union citizens to join the UK Army or Army Reserve, I want the UK to allow EU citizens to join the Army or Army Reserve in UK.

I believe a lot of EU citizens who permanently live or have settled status in UK want to join the Army or Army Reserve but at this moment they're denied this.,

Require online review sites to prevent fraudulent reviews., Businesses have suffered enough through the COVID-19 Pandemic. The freedom for people to post fraudulent or false reviews on sites such as Tripadvisor or Google has been used to harass and damage the reputations of businesses at a time that should be about business growth., The Government should create legal requirements for review sites to require them to check for proof of visiting or using a business prior to leaving a review (such as providing proof of receipt or a code given at the time of service). This should prevent fraudulent attacks on businesses by competitors or individuals posting false reviews, allowing businesses to better adapt to real life issues and grow appropriately, rather than being subject to bullying cyber attacks.

Remove Ofsted’s involvement in counselling services for adopted adults., Currently adopted adults in UK have to follow rules set out by Ofsted to access counselling services. This exacerbates the feeling of being different and infantilises adult adoptees, something many adoptees have experienced throughout their lives. Give back choice to adult adoptees who want therapy., Currently adult adoptees have to find a therapist who is part of an adoption support agency and Ofsted require these agencies to keep records of these adults who are seeking therapy, why? These regulations have been further tightened recently, making it even harder for adults affected by adoption to find support. Adult adoptees feel stigmatised by Ofsted’s unnecessary involvement.We need to find a more suitable way of regulating therapy for adopted adults which makes accessing support easier.

Ban private schools , Private schools should be nationalised and converted into state schools. I believe that private schools nurture class division. If we are a forward thinking nation, private schools should have no place in society., Finland banned for-profit basic education. Since then, I believe Finland has seen huge societal improvements (naturally) given the levels of freely available education.
I believe that we are run by a class that perceives themselves to be better, together with an ability to buy their way through life.

Conduct a review into the family court service CAFCAS, A review should be set up to look at the services and conduct of CAFCAS in family court cases. The review should result in recommendations for reforming the CAFCAS service to improve its work, ensure that decisions are evidence based and fully take into account the voices of children., We believe CAFCAS has become heavily outdated and out of touch with family matters in England; it appears to be unreliable and based on the personal opinions of those officers investigating. Children's voices are rarely heard.

Impose sanctions on the US until it bans general firearm ownership for public, Human rights are being violated on a weekly basis in the US by gun holders, UK citizens and residents with family in the US need to wake up every day to check if there was a mass shooting in the vicinity to where their family live., Strong action and pressure is needed from the international community. We cannot hold relationships with countries where their own citizens human rights are not respected.

Require online games have child-only servers to help protect children, Bring in a law that gaming companies hosting online games need to provide child-only servers for UK users, with access limited to under 16s. The Government should require ID and age checks to ensure these servers are only used by children., There is a huge problem with grooming via online gaming and action is needed to create a safer way for children to play games online.
 
We believe that requiring child-only servers, with rigorous age and ID checks, would better protect children from online dangers.

Investigate Banks who have closed customers bank accounts without  just cause., Bring the banks (especially Natwest) under the law to protect the rights of all customers from the poorest to the richest. Banking conitions should be define by the law not the banks, who seem to be able to change their terms with impunity., There seems to be no legislation in place to safeguard customers from their accounts being closed or protect them from the hardship caused by doing so. Banks should exist to provide a service to the public and there should be legislation in place to protect their customers from being without banking services

Extend hate crime offences to include targeting people based on their sex, Make people being attacked or victimised for their sex a hate crime, as is already the case for (e.g.) race and religion., Sex is a protected characteristic in the Equality Act. Hate crime offences already exist for where people are attacked because of other protected characteristics such as race, sexual orientation, or religion. All the protected characteristics should have equal rights. It is also important because women are attacked every day simply because of their sex and making this a hate crime could give more information on how to tackle it. Nobody should be hurt because they are a woman or a man.

Establish a not-for-profit state owned energy provider, Create a Government, state owned energy provider, set low prices to just cover costs. If competitors want to stay in business they must reduce prices to compete or fold. No extra expense for buying back franchises etc. Just compete and help our own people., Certain things like utilities should be offered at honest prices to the public throughout the UK. It is simply not fair or decent to let any businesses profiteer on the back of making ordinary people suffer financial hardships when it is not necessary.
A government-run utility company could offer mass employment and honest prices whilst making a modest profit to cover costs. This would also negate the constant tax incentives or payments to help people cope and force honest competition.

Negotiate and agree with the EU to ease access of UK Musicians to tour Europe., To negotiate and agree with the European Union, to allow fair and unrestricted access for UK musicians to tour its member countries and perform live. To create a dialogue which will deliver a reciprocated system to allow the entry, travel and performance rights of UK musicians in Europe., Since BREXIT UK musicians face an unfair, inefficient, costly and time consuming system that creates significant obstacles and difficulties to UK musicians to tour EU member countries. This is not only unfair and frustrating for the performers, but is equally so for the millions of music fans who wish to see our talented musicians perform across Europe. A new, fair and efficient agreement to facilitate this, will benefit both the UK and Europe and promote cultural and financial benefits for all

Ban all non-UK residents from owning more than two residential properties, The government needs to immediately prevent any non-UK resident investors (private or commercial) from owning more than two 2 UK residential properties., The younger generation of the UK simply cannot get on the housing ladder. We believe this difficulty is not caused by a lack of housing stock, but by an increase in residential property ownership by non-UK residents. This needs to be minimised so that UK residents & families can look to buy their own homes.

Extend the Help to Buy Equity Loan to people who have already owned property, Currently the Help to Buy Equity Loan is only available to first-time buyers. We want this requirement to be removed, so people who currently or have previously owned a property are eligible for this scheme.,

Commission a review into police handling of allegations of spiking, With cases of drink spiking reaching new highs every year, a review into how the police handle allegations of spiking by victims, including gathering and assessing evidence, is vital. We are concerned police do not place enough priority on properly looking at the evidence and making arrests., Currently, victims are spiked, hospital staff say to inform the police, but if the police argue there isn’t enough evidence (despite potential evidence including lists of attendees, CCTV footage, and witnesses), then no action is taken. 
 
This also means potential medical evidence can be missed. As a victim of spiking, medical staff told me they couldn’t do a toxicology report without the police’s involvement. However, the police closed my case and I didn't have my blood tested. Cooperation between medical staff and the police must therefore also be reviewed, so improvement can be made.

Apply to join the European Union Single Market, Rejoin the EU single market. This would fulfil the promise of being outside the European Union while promoting trade and cooperation across nations., While there was a referendum on the question of EU trade block membership in 2016, many things have changed since then. Critically, recent figures show that many voters have changed their minds https://www.statista.com/statistics/987347/brexit-opinion-poll/. Re-joining the single market would ultimately allow the UK to mitigate the cost of living crisis and foster future cooperation.

Fund annual health checks for all adults, We want the Government to put in place funding for annual health checks for all adults, to help identify health conditions at an early stage., People are encouraged to have regular dental check-ups and eye tests, but there are no regular checks for a person's wider health.
 
Many health conditions could be identified earlier, or better monitored and treated, with regular health checks. If patients are invited once yearly to a health check, healthcare practitioners can check overall health, and also advise on how to avoid health risks, such as obesity.
 
Prevention is better than cure, but we as a nation are not grasping this. A simple health check could save many lives and we believe would be cost effective to the NHS.

Stronger sentences for online abuse, and fund mental health support, The Government should increase sentences for online abuse, including gaslighting and catfishing. They should also fund more mental health support for victims, and for those who work with vulnerable people including the police, social workers, charity workers, and emergency services., I am fighting for a Law called ‘Gem’s Law’ to help reduce job anxiety/overall anxiety on social media platforms and more people are heard and kept at peace. I want people to feel listened to, be able to be themselves online therefore people do not feel the need to scam/fraud, preventing catfishing/victim numbers from soaring. I want to fight for Freedom and Human Rights to impact people’s mental health for the better.

Change the age of consent to 18, The age of consent should be changed to 18 rather than 16, as a 16 year old is still considered a child in many respects. , The law of consent says that a person who is 16 or older may have sexual intercourse with anyone who is also 16 or older, but I don’t believe they are mature enough to decide this.

A person aged 16 cannot legally send an explicit image of themselves as such images would be considered 'child porn' . With this logic, a 16 year old is considered a child, but is legally able to have sexual intercourse with someone over the age of 18 (an adult) . These laws contradict one another. If a 16 year old is a child according to another law, then how is it protecting anyone?
Get us out of the ECHR immediately, Get us out of the ECHR, This country overwhelmingly voted for Brexit and to become a sovereign nation and not to be dictated to by the EU and it’s supporters

Automatically grant equal access rights following separation, The Government should change the law so both parents are granted equal (50-50) access rights to their child when they legally separate or divorce. They should also be required to agree a contact agreement based on a 50-50 split as a condition of being granted legal separation or divorce., This change should ensure parents have the legal right to access even if their ex-partner tries to refuse access. Family breakdown costs the taxpayer an estimated £47 billion per year and the process could be more effectively managed. It is too easy for mothers to withhold their children from their fathers. This is a widespread problem as there are an estimated 2.9 million households in the UK with a lone parent, the vast majority of which are mothers. It can cost tens of thousands of pounds and several years to get access. The cost and time is needless abuse on fathers and children.

Place a complete ban on the sale and use of disposable BBQ’s in the UK, We support moves to ban disposable BBQ’s in environmentally vulnerable areas. Limited restrictions will not stop them being used or brought into these spaces. This also does nothing to counter the damage they do outside these areas.  We are calling for an outright ban on their use and sale in the UK, Whether it is massive environmental damage, life changing injuries & deaths, food poisoning or single use waste that comes with disposable BBQ’s, there are simply too many issues, risks and dangers when buying and using them. 

It’s not enough to stop their sale ‘near’ beaches or moorland. 

It’s not enough to dismiss the countless problems and blame people for being ‘irresponsible’. 

Disposable BBQ’s themselves carry too many risks and our call is for them to be banned completely.

Seek working holiday visa for young Britons to live and work in EEA countries, For the Government to seek to agree a deal with all EEA member states for young Britons to be able to access a working holiday visa. Agreements are already in place for Canada, Australia, New Zealand etc. However, since Brexit opportunities, to work and live in the EEA are limited., Estimates indicate over 70% of under 25s voted to remain a part of the EU. The opportunity for young people to work and travel almost anywhere in Europe is something many people can now only dream of rather than turn it into a reality, even when many young people voted to remain.
 
Whilst we all respect democracy and vote leave won, I believe young Britons should still get a chance to experience living and working in an EEA country of their choice whilst young.

Hold a Referendum on re-joining the EU, Brexit is the biggest disaster any government has ever negotiated., The Tory government failed in its basic duty knowingly, it also knowingly lied in its campaign and published false statements. 

Brexit is destroying the very fabric of UK trade, business, social harmony, prosperity and freedom.

Do what’s right take us back into the EU and give us a voice once again in Europe.

Review how the NHS determine whether people are a healthy weight, Currently the most common method to check if someone is a a healthy weight is body mass index (BMI). However, we believe this index is unsatisfactory, and can exacerbate or even lead to body dysmorphia, because it is based solely on height and weight., The Government should review how the NHS determine whether people are a healthy weight, with a view to establishing if it is still suitable for the body mass index (BMI) to be used for this purpose.
 
This review should look at the impact current practice can have on patients' mental health, especially for those who suffer from body-image issues.

Scrap university fees for doctors, nurses, etc providing they finish the course., I believe the government should scrap all university fees for Doctors, Nurses, Paramedics, etc and only charge them if they do not complete the course and work for a minimum terms eg the length of their course., This is because health care professionals hold our country together. They dedicate their lives to helping the whole country and without them we are nothing. They should not have to pay tens of thousands of pounds to serve our country in the amazing and dedicated way that they do. My brother is currently attending St George’s University to get his Medical degree and we as a family are having to pay for all of his fees due to him already having a degree funded although he is going to be a doctor.

Limit rent charges on new shared ownership properties to ground rent, We believe the current shared ownership system does not work. The rent and mortgage combined can make it unaffordable for many, especially younger people. The rent element should constitute ground rent only, and not a rental charge for the share of the property the tenant does not own., With rising mortgage rates and inflation contributing to increased rent, many low-income families are struggling to make shared ownership work. We believe this step could help tackle the housing crisis the Government is facing, and make shared ownership properties more affordable.

Provide free parking for all NHS staff on site, Provide free parking for all NHS staff at their place of work, All Key workers necessary to run a hospital should be provided with safe parking on site to ease the existing financial stress on an already stressful role in society. We should be taking more care of the people who care for us.

Require all electric vehicles in the UK to use a standardised modular battery, We want the Government to require all electric and hybrid vehicles sold or manufactured in the UK to use a standardised, modular design for an interchangeable main traction battery., Battery degradation is one of the major factors limiting the usable life of electric and hybrid cars. Replacement batteries are expensive and usually only supplied by car manufacturers. If all vehicles shared a common and modular battery design, a market could exist for replacement batteries with many manufacturers providing similar and interchangeable products. This should bring down the cost for consumers, extend the life of vehicles on the road and reduce the environmental impact of motoring.

Ban school branding on shirts, polo shirts, trousers and skirts for all schools., Research has shown that compulsory school uniform costs up to £300 per child, per year. Schools are increasingly requiring logos & school/house colours on items which could otherwise be bought in supermarkets at a hugely reduced cost. While most areas have uniform exchanges it is all unecessary., If you have a child who requires a different fit of trousers for example (plus fit/slim fit/tall) this isn't always possible with compulsory branding, same for skirts and tops. Our local high school said the logo was introduced due to the length of skirts. The skirts are now shorter than ever as girls can only buy the specific school branded skirts, 2 lengths isn't always adequate!

Ban the production of virgin (new) plastics immediately, The Government needs to implement action to tackle plastic waste. Plastics are ending up in the bellies of sea animals and birds and ending up in our (Human) food cycle. By banning the production of new plastics, this should force manufacturers to use more environmentally friendly materials., The Government needs to implement action to stop the production of new virgin plastics and force the use of environmentally friendly materials already in circulation, to help the fight against climate change.

Ban commercial donkey rides, Ban commercial donkey rides. It is an outdated practice. The donkeys are often forced to work long hours, often without sufficient shade during heatwaves., It's animal abuse and outdated.

Voucher scheme for those with Coeliacs Disease for gluten-free food, Those with Coeliac Disease need to avoid gluten, but some PCTs have stopped prescribing Gluten Free food as it’s too costly for the NHS. I would like the Government to give those with Coeliacs Disease a monthly voucher for gluten-free food, to help them maintain a healthy diet., With the cost of living crisis, Gluten Free food was already more expensive than regular food, and now costs have increased more.

Italy has a scheme funded by the government where those with Coeliacs Disease receive vouchers specifically for gluten-free food (eg. bread, pasta, flours etc.). If there was a similar scheme for those who have Coeliacs Disease in the UK this should help save the NHS from prescribing this food. Vouchers could be based on age & how much gluten free food they require.

Seek to join Schengen to ease travel, The UK needs to join Schengen so the UK public can travel freely in Europe again., The UK travellers to Europe should not face the restrictions that exist currently. We need to join Schengen again and go back to freedom of travel.

Give businesses the right to opt out of Business Improvements District levies, Many businesses are being required to pay levy rates into Business Improvement Districts (BIDs), which can be extortionate, and of which many don’t see a penny back. Some businesses have closed down because they simply can’t afford to pay up with these levies., Businesses are struggling and we believe yet another tax is no help to saving our high streets and protecting local businesses. The Government needs to give businesses the right to opt out of these levies, so those who can afford to pay the levy can to keep BIDs operating, and protecting small businesses who are struggling at the same time.

Stop courts being able to grant care orders based on risk of future suffering, We believe current laws on removing children from parents are outdated and unjust. Currently a court can grant a care order removing children from their parents if they are 'likely to suffer harm'. This can mean children can be removed even if they have come to no harm. We believe this is wrong., The laws need to be changed. The amount of children going into care has increased substantially in the last ten years. Some parents are going abroad to avoid the social services because they believe there is no alternative.

Remove UK signature from amended FCDO policy statement, The UK Government needs to revoke its signature on the amended FCDO statement issued this July, on freedom of religion or belief and gender equality. This statement removed the written commitment to uphold women's "sexual and reproductive health and rights, bodily autonomy.", "Bodily autonomy" is the right to make decisions over one's own life & future. It is being empowered to make informed choices. 15 countries that signed the original statement have not signed the amended statement. Why did the UK Government sign for this change, this lack of written commitment? Why are they not standing for women's rights? They need to revoke their signature - now - before women's rights are written out entirely. It only ever starts with one change.

Stop shark being sold under misleading names in the UK, Defra's Commercial Designations of Fish allows 46 shark species to be sold under 6 generic names in UK chippies and fishmongers (e.g. Rock Salmon). These include Critically Endangered sharks. We ask that shark must instead be sold under common names to enable consumers to make ethical choices., Sharks are critical to oceans.

46 (often rare) sharks can be sold as Rock Salmon, Rock Eel, Dogfish, Flake, Huss or Rigg. 94 DNA samples showed an 86% chance of eating Spiny Dogfish in a chippy when ordering fish listed under these names.

The IUCN Red List assessment found that Spiny Dogfish stock in the NE Atlantic was Critically Endangered, and Vulnerable to Extinction globally.

Tope - Critically Endangered globally - is sold under these names too. For comparison, orangutans and gorillas are also Critically Endangered.

Renationalise all industries that were publicly owned and restrict future sales, We want the Government to renationalise all industries that were previously publicly owned. There should also be new restrictions on the sale of public assets, removing the ability for Government to sell/put to tender, public infrastructure, without a public vote., We want the Government to renationalise all sold infrastructure, dating back to 1979, and restrict the sale of public sector organisations to private hands.

Appoint an Adult Mental Health Ambassador and Adult Mental Health Group, Mental health and the lack of a joined up approach and timely services is a major issue.
 
The Government has appointed a Youth Mental Health Ambassador - so the importance and impact of such a role is already realised. We believe there should also be an Adult Mental Health Ambassador., If the Government are taking advice in relation to youth mental health they should also consider adult mental health.
 
There is a Mental Health in Education Action Group which the Youth Ambassador sits on and we believe there is a need for there to be an action group in relation to adult mental health also.

Legislate to ban commercial wooden pallets treated with highly toxic chemicals, We ask the Government to ban all commercial wooden pallets which are treated with highly toxic chemicals. There are other eco-friendly pallets available, and there is no justification why any industry should still be using these wooden pallets for logistical transport and distribution., People may think wooden pallets are safe to burn domestically, but PM2.5 emissions are one of the most dangerous pollutants to human health. Banning wooden pallets treated with toxic chemicals should benefit the environment, public health and NHS.

More for information see the links below:

https://www.blf.org.uk/sites/default/files/Ambient%20air%20pollution_levelling%20up%20lung%20health.pdf

https://www.london.gov.uk/sites/default/files/pm2.5_in_london_october19.pdf

Fund private mental health care for people with mental health issues, Too many people struggle to access mental health support through the NHS, and we want the Government to fund private mental health care - including counselling and psychological therapies - for people with mental health issues, so they don't have to wait for support through the NHS.,

National Planning Policy Framework to prioritise locally-owned businesses., Calling for the National Planning Policy Framework to prioritise existing locally-owned businesses across all local authority's regeneration plans., It’s imperative for locally owned business owners to be considered in all matters of planning and regeneration. It should be mandatory for all developers to adhere to new versions of Local Planning policy ensuring developers provide all local businesses a relocation strategy and give careful consideration to small businesses and the wider community it serves.

Leave the European Convention on Human Rights and the Council of Europe., Exit ECHR and the Council of Europe. Many people who voted for Brexit assumed leaving the EU meant leaving all European supranational institutions. As an independent nation state and island nation, the United Kingdom must have primacy over outside bodies in this key area., Exiting ECHR also means leaving the Council of Europe, another supranational entity that most UK citizens would not be aware of.

We want Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) to be a protected profession., To put this into legislation, Some people are saying that they do CBT when they can not. CBT is a highly effective treatment for anxiety disorders. Not protecting the name means the public will be out at risk.

Commission an independent audit into spending on NHS Test and Trace, I want the Government to fully account for public money spent on NHS Test and Trace, a programme that had a £37 billion budget for its first two years, and for which there is little evidence of benefits being delivered., Because the Government should be held to account when it spends gargantuan sums of taxpayers' money.

Stop charging double vehicle tax for the month in which a vehicle is sold, Amidst the cost of living crisis the Government is charging double vehicle tax for cars bought and sold in the middle of the month. This is absolutely deplorable. The Government should reform vehicle tax so it is calculated to the day, rather than having to be paid for the full calendar month., At present the person selling a motor vehicle and the person buying the same motor vehicle must pay full road tax for the month it is sold/purchased. This is because drivers must pay road tax for the full month for any period they are responsible for a vehicle. This means the Government is charging vehicle tax twice for the same month for the same vehicle. Enough is enough. This must stop now.

Require businesses selling e-cigarettes to offer recycling of used products, We want the Government to create legal requirements for businesses that sell e-cigarettes to offer to take used products and arrange for these to be recycled., There is going to be far too much battery waste in landfill and not recycled. The Government should take action to improve recycling rates for e-cigarettes.

Make the resale of event tickets for more than face value illegal., For major sports events, music concerts, etc., tickets are sold online.
Touts use automated software to buy tickets en masse, for the sole purpose of reselling them at inflated prices.
Mass buying of tickets, for the purpose of reselling at more than their face value, must be made illegal., An example:
For the Chris Eubank Jr v Conor Benn boxing event, tickets went on sale at a specific time. From that time, 20000 tickets were sold out in 10 minutes - which is impossible unless they were being bought en masse.
Another 10 minutes later, thousands of tickets appeared for resale at three or four times their face value, such that fans had no choice but to pay the inflated prices.
The same happens for other events, e.g. music concerts. This blatant profiteering must be stopped.

To exempt all care residences from energy price increases, If the Government were to remove  the financial burden and consequent worry of energy price increases from all those requiring care, regardless of where they access that care, it would be a significant indicator that the nation’s leaders are genuinely concerned for society’s vulnerable people., The pandemic united people across the country in a shared endeavour to keep our respective communities safe. One action was to remain at home. Those same communities feel threatened further by financial hardship - will they stay indoors this time, or might they take their frustrations and fears onto the streets?

Increase the LISA £450,000 first time buyer price cap in line with house prices., Increase the price cap of £450,000 for first time buyers hoping to take advantage of using their LISA contributions towards their first home. The price cap (Set in 2015) has been frozen since its introduction and should be increased in line with the increase in house prices we've seen since then., Its becoming harder and harder for first time buyer to get on the property ladder in the UK, made even harder by inflation, cost of living crises, fuel poverty and the fear of recession. UK house prices have increased by at least 23% since the LISA product was launched. The £450k limit has remained unchanged for the last 7 years while potential first time buyers saved for their first home through an LISA. A useful tool with increasingly unrealistic restrictions. This cap should be nearer £560,000.

Government must not move UK embassy in Israel to Jerusalem., We urge the Government not move the UK embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Juresleum.

If the UK is serious about its commitment for last peace in the Middle East it must not move the UK embassy. 

The UK Government does not recognise Juresleum as being the capital of Israel., On 6th December 2017, former Prime Minster Theresa May said:

We disagree with the US decision to move its embassy to Jerusalem and recognise Jerusalem as the Israeli capital before a final status agreement. We believe it is unhelpful in terms of prospects for peace in the region. The British Embassy to Israel is based in Tel Aviv and we have no plans to move it.

No status agreement has been agreed, moving the embassy at this time will mean favouring one side over the other
Review the review board of the rugby football league rfl, To stop the biased rulings of the rfl and to stop it ruining the game, Sort out for tha national game of rugby league how it is run

Remove 3% stamp duty surcharge for property owners buying a permanent residence, This should apply to buyers owning existing property (in the UK or overseas) but who are buying a property to be their main home. For a £425k property buyers with an existing property pay £21.5k instead of £0 for first time buyers or £8.75k for those moving home. It should be same moving home., Examples would be young professionals living in expensive areas (for ex. London) and who couldn’t afford to buy in their areas and who decided to buy property elsewhere, for a second home or to buy to let, until they could afford to buy their main home.
 
Another example would be people who have inherited a property but do not live in that property and want to buy their main home. They may not have the ability to sell the property, especially if it is shared with other members of their family.

Keep retained EU environmental laws until equal or stronger UK laws introduced, The Retained EU Law (Revocation & Reform) Bill will remove EU-derived law protecting air, water, wildlife, land and waste in 2023. We want these laws to be retained until replacement legislation is passed which delivers equal or stronger protection for nature than retained EU law., UK governments in the past decade have variously promised to be "the greenest government ever" and "to be the first generation that leaves the environment in a better state than that in which we inherited it". But the EU Law Bill risks creating a "gun-at-the-head" deadline for replacing retained EU law, rather than removing retained laws when Parliament has formulated and passed equal or stronger UK law. We believe spending valuable Parliamentary time on the latter would be the better option.

Consider replacing the tax system with an automated tax on all transactions, Commission a feasibility study to assess the effects of replacing the existing tax system with an automated tax on every UK financial transaction. The Government should publish a report showing the likely affects such a change would have on the UK economy, and whether it will implement this change.,

Create financial penalties for property buyers who pull out of purchases, We want the Government to impose financial penalties on property purchasers who pull out of a purchase after submitting a final offer, unless there is a good reason. The fine should be paid to the seller., Buyers pulling out after submitting an offer can have huge financial implications for sellers, and affect people's mental health.
 
Buyers should only be able to pull out of a sale if there is a good reason, such as serious faults being found following an inspection, not just because they change their mind or find another property.

Negotiate with the EU for mutual visa-free six month visit rights, Seek to negotiate with the EU, mutual rights to visa-free visits for six months. Currently, EU visitors already have these rights when visiting the UK, but UK visitors to the EU are limited to 90 days every 180 days., We believe it is only fair that UK citizens visiting the EU have equal rights to EU citizens visiting the UK.

Make it illegal to buy or sell nitrous oxide (laughing gas), There are far too many cases where young people have ended up in hospital, or even died, after taking nitrous oxide.

We believe this gas should be banned, so it cannot legally be bought or sold in the UK., Many children see nitrous oxide as safe and legal, and far too many end up being admitted to hospital after inhaling nitrous oxide.

An outright ban would make it clear that this gas is dangerous, and should help tackle its use by children.

Extend any cap on social housing rent increases to shared ownership properties, We want the Government to extend any cap on social housing rent increases in 2023 to shared ownership properties., We in Shared Ownership need help during the cost of living crisis. We are facing high rent increases this coming year, and need a new cap introduced to protect us.
 
Rent for shared ownership tenants can be increased by up to RPI + 0.5%. RPI is already above the rate of CPI, so many tenants are facing unaffordable rent increases. We require the same care and consideration for rent caps as people in social housing.
 
We are asking the Government to cap rents for shared owners at the same rate that housing association tenants are capped for 2023.

Withdraw the Retained EU Law (Revocation and Reform) Bill, The Government has introduced legislation that would revoke most EU retained law at the end of 2023. This includes regulations and legislation on areas such as workers’ rights, transport, finance and environmental protection.

Such changes must be subject to consultation with ALL stakeholders., Brexit was touted as the enabler for the UK to be ‘the’ place to do business; to enable us to be more responsive to change. The planned Retained EU Law (Revocation and Reform) Bill is the next step of the Government's plans to cut perceived red tape. Changes to existing laws cannot go unchallenged.

This bill represents a potentially apocalyptic bonfire of essential, hard-won regulations and legislation, and it could further propel this country in an unedifying race to the bottom.

Allow nut allergy sufferers into the UK Armed Forces, To allow sufferers of any peanut/ nut allergy to join any of the UK forces PROVIDING they sign a disclaimer in the event they may suffer an attack., Currently if he/she develop an allergy whilst in the armed forces he/she won’t get medically removed but will have their tours shortened.
I want the government to allow sufferers of any peanut/ nut allergy to join any of the UK forces PROVIDING they sign disclaimer in the event they may suffer an attack. Also if he/she can provide proof they haven’t had to use an EpiPen in the last 2years.

Hold a referendum on rejoining the EU following the outcome Brexit agreement, As the public were refused the opportunity of a referendum as to the content of the UK's exit deal with EU and now having experience the negative outcomes as a result of leaving the EU, we want a referendum on rejoining the EU., Following loss of free trade, free movement and all the previous benefits of being part of the EU, we want to rejoin the EU. Many parts of our lives have been made more difficult following Brexit, and the promised benefits of leaving the EU have not materialised.
 
The financial / political crisis has made the situation even more acute. The £37 billion divorce bill is such a waste of our money. If we can’t have a general election at least allow a referendum for the public to vote on whether they wish to rejoin the the EU.

Update hate crime action plan and increase actions to tackle hate crime, The Government's hate crime action plan ran from 2016 to 2020, and has not been replaced. We want the Government to produce an updated hate crime action plan, and introduce new duties for local authorities and the police to tackle hate crime., Police Recorded Hate Crime (HC) in England and Wales 155,641 up 26% Race HC 109,843 up 19% Religious HC 8,370 up 37% Homophobic HC 26,152 up 41% Disability HC 14,242 up 43% Transphobic HC 4,355 up 56%.There should be no place for hate in the UK.
 
The Government should prepare a comprehensive hate crime action plan, and update legislation to create statutory duties for the police and local authorities to produce local hate crime action plans.
 
We also call on the Government to support initiatives like National Hate Crime Awareness Week and to actively encourage the authorities, key partners and communities affected by hate crime to work together to tackle all forms of Hate Crime across the UK.

Increase funding to ensure all adults and children have access to a dentist., I cannot find a dentist with capacity to take my family on (after existing practice closed). This is unacceptable. There are no NHS places and even private schemes have waiting lists (and unaffordable one off registration fees)., The Government must review how dentistry is funded and run. The current situation is a disaster.
